metaculus.access: BrowserOS Neo; full retained page read
findings: MiniBench normally starts on alternate Mondays, with roughly 60 questions.
Three-hour windows; one forecast per question.
No owner forecasts, preview-based tuning or reruns of unwanted answers. Closed-question development is permitted.
Private comments may become public.
Solo-founder prize classification does not grant commercial API rights. Human-owned registration precedes entry.

metaculus.access: BrowserOS Neo; API 2.0.0 description, numeric schema and atomic-request example read; static YAML download timed out and a CLI retrieval returned HTTP 403. No further download was attempted. A native dialog was not observed or controlled.
findings: Authenticated access required; a hidden field may be present as null.
Post IDs differ from underlying question IDs. Group children retain their own question IDs.
Commercial use needs a written agreement; model development/evaluation has separate written-permission conditions.
Numeric submissions require a 201-point CDF on the exact question scale.
POST /api/questions/bulk-forecast-comment/ accepts forecasts and private comments atomically; 201 means saved, 400 means none saved, 403 means acting-account permission denied.
No API call, token, credential inspection or actual request was made by the rehearsal.

metaculus.access: BrowserOS Neo public terms read after the closed-question observations were collected
findings: General automated website collection and redistribution are not granted by the ordinary terms. Official API/Metaculus-provided automated interfaces have their own terms.
No future question acquisition through Neo is part of the delivery; use an allowed official interface after account/access setup.
The raw observations remain in the local item result. The clean delivery branch excludes them.
No training, outcome-based evaluation, externally scored forecast, commercial permission or terms acceptance is claimed.

metaculus.access: BrowserOS Neo; tournament and Bot Participation Rules read
findings: Q4 2026 tournament uses spot scoring at each question close.
One entry is allowed, either as a bot or as a person.
Questions include rolling numeric groups: futures return spreads, yields, volatility and company results. Spot direction/touch/target-before-stop forecasts do not supply those distributions.
